feature: Sandbox isolation for eval session runner
problem: CursorClient.launch_bridge() inherits os.environ, so any server the agent starts inside the sandbox exposes CURSOR_API_KEY and other secrets via environment variables to localhost
proposed_solution: Two-layer defense: (1) strip sensitive env vars from os.environ before launch_bridge, restore after in finally block; (2) enable SDK SandboxOptions for filesystem/shell/network isolation
acceptance_criteria: AC1: SENSITIVE_ENV_VARS list includes CURSOR_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN
AC2: _strip_sensitive_env() removes all SENSITIVE_ENV_VARS from os.environ and returns stashed values
AC3: _restore_sensitive_env() restores stashed values in a finally block — always runs even on exception
AC4: SandboxOptions(enabled=True) is passed to LocalAgentOptions by default
AC5: --no-sandbox CLI flag disables sandbox with warning in help text
AC6: api_key is still passed explicitly to agents.create() — not relying on env inheritance
AC7: dry-run output shows sandbox status
AC8: File compiles cleanly (py_compile) and passes make validate
edge_cases: EC1: If a SENSITIVE_ENV_VAR is not set in the parent env, _strip_sensitive_env should not fail
EC2: If the bridge crashes between strip and restore, the finally block must still restore vars
verification_method: Read session_runner.py, verify all ACs by code inspection. Run py_compile and make validate. Check that stash/restore wraps the entire bridge lifecycle with finally.
